rooms.1900: A tall gate of black wrought iron stands in an arch of crumbling brick, one leaf hanging open on a single rusted hinge. A worn path leads out through the grass toward the old cathedral's churchyard, and the smell of turned earth drifts in on the draught. The way north runs on through the arch to the front yard, between pillars topped with weathered stone urns. A bell-pull dangles from its chain beside the gate, and it swings a little though nothing touches it.
rooms.1901: Weeds as high as your waist choke what was once a formal garden, and a cracked gravel drive curls between them toward the house. A dry fountain stands off to one side, its basin green with scum and its stone cherub missing its face. Shuttered windows stare down from the great house, and in one of them a curtain twitches as you look. The front door stands north, studded with nails and painted a dead black, and the gate lies back south.
rooms.1902: A grand foyer rises two floors under a chandelier so thick with cobwebs that it hangs like a great grey nest, and the black and white tiles beneath are dull with dust. Family portraits climb the walls in heavy frames, and their painted eyes follow you across the floor. A wide staircase curves up to the gallery, and a low door beneath it leads down to the cellar. Arches open north to the kitchen, east to the living room and west to the sitting room, while the front door lies south.
rooms.1907: Cold iron pots hang from rusted hooks above a vast black range, and the long table is scarred by a century of cleavers. A cold spot lingers by the hearth, where the air bites at your fingers and a pot lid rattles faintly on nothing. A glass door east opens on the greenhouse, the servants' corridor runs on west, and the grand foyer lies south.
rooms.1906: Dead plants fill the greenhouse in brittle brown ranks, their clay pots cracked and their leaves rattling at the slightest breath of air. Grimy glass panes make a grey roof overhead, several of them broken, and a bench of rotted seedling trays sags under a litter of dry soil. A vine as thick as your wrist has strangled the iron frame, and its pale blossoms are still faintly, wrongly, alive. The only way out is the glass door west, back into the kitchen.
rooms.1908: A plain low corridor of whitewash and bare boards, where servants once hurried unseen between the kitchen and the rooms off the passage. A board of little brass bells hangs over the doors, each one labelled with the name of a room, and now and then one trembles and rings with no hand upon its wire. Doors open north and south, the kitchen lies back east, and the corridor runs on west to its end.
rooms.1913: The housekeeper's room is tidy still, with a big ledger desk, a hook-board of numbered keys and a narrow bed made up with a patched grey quilt. A little window looks onto a blank wall, and the lamp on the desk is full of oil though the wick is black. The cold is sharpest by the bed, where the quilt keeps settling as if someone had just risen from it. A door south leads back to the corridor, and an opening west gives onto a water closet.
rooms.1914: A narrow water closet tiled in white and blue, the glaze crazed with age and a long crack running down the basin. The pull chain swings gently though the air is still, and water drips somewhere behind the wall in a slow count. A door east leads back to the housekeeper's room, and an opening west gives onto the butler's room. The smell of wet plaster is thick here.
rooms.1915: The butler's room is a spare, upright place, with a tall narrow bed, a wardrobe of black coats and a silver cabinet standing open and empty. A plate-polishing board is propped against the wall, and a ring of old stains on the table marks where a lamp or decanter long stood. Faint footsteps cross the floor when you are still, pausing before the wardrobe. A door east leads to the water closet, and the way south returns to the end of the corridor.
rooms.1909: The corridor ends here at a blank wall hung with a single cracked mirror, in which the whitewash looks greyer and the doors look farther apart than they are. Doors stand north and south, and the passage runs back east toward the kitchen. A smell of boiled cabbage and soap lingers in the cold, and from the walls comes a soft knocking, like a hand tapping to be let out.
rooms.1910: A chef's private room, smelling of old spices and rancid fat, with a narrow bed, a cabinet of copper-bottomed pans and a tattered book of recipes chained to the wall. Knife marks score the table, deep and many, and a stain darkens the floorboards beneath it. The air is close and oddly warm, as if a fire burned in the next room. A door east leads to a water closet, and the way north returns to the end of the corridor.
rooms.1911: This water closet is small and mean, whitewashed brick with a wooden seat and a tin basin, built for the kitchen staff and not the family. A rusted bucket stands in a corner, and a window no bigger than a book is blocked with grime. The walls are scrawled with names and tallies in pencil, some very old. A door east opens on the cook's room, and the chef's room lies through the opening west.
rooms.1912: The cook's room is cramped and warm-smelling, hung with strings of dried herbs gone to dust. A rocking chair sits before a little iron stove, and an apron on a peg has a sooty handprint on its front that grows no fainter however long you stare. The ticking of a clock fills the silence, though there is no clock to be seen. A way north returns to the servants' corridor, and the water closet lies west.
rooms.1905: Sheeted furniture crowds the living room like patient ghosts, and a vast stone hearth gapes cold behind a screen of rotting embroidery. Dust lies thick on the mantel, broken only by the clear outline of a missing clock. A faded carpet shows the track of a rocking chair that creaks in the corner whenever you turn your back. The only way out is the wide arch back west to the foyer.
rooms.1903: A grand piano stands in the bay of this sitting room, its lid raised, and every so often a few slow notes of a half-remembered waltz drift out though no hands touch the keys. Moth-eaten armchairs face a cold fireplace, and the wallpaper hangs in long damp tongues. A door west leads to the library, an opening north gives onto the dining room, and the foyer lies back east.
rooms.1916: A long table laid for twelve is furred with dust, every plate in its place and every glass still holding a dark crust at the bottom. Candle stubs burn low in the silver candelabra, though no one has lit them in years. Chairs are pushed back at odd angles, as if the diners rose all at once and fled. Only the doorway south to the sitting room breaks the wall of dark panelling.
rooms.1904: Shelves climb to the ceiling, bowed with crumbling books, and a rolling ladder is stuck fast on its rail. Cold gathers in the corner by the globe, and the pages of an open volume on the reading desk turn over slowly, one at a time. A narrow door in the shelves to the north stands ajar on a hidden stair, and the sitting room lies back east.
rooms.1927: Narrow steps spiral down behind the library shelves, and the walls are close enough to brush both shoulders. Cobwebs hang in grey veils, parted in the middle as though someone had passed this way not long ago. The air is chill and still, with a faint smell of damp earth. A door south leads back to the library, and the stair drops down to a hidden room.
rooms.1928: A small windowless chamber, bare but for a rotted table, a child's chair and heaps of mouldering paper. Letters in a feminine hand are pinned across the walls, scrawled over and over with the same few words. The cold is deep, and your breath hangs before you. The stair climbs up to the library above, and there is no other way out.
rooms.1917: The grand staircase sweeps up in a broad curve, its red carpet worn to threads and its banister carved with climbing roses. A tall clock halfway up has stopped at a quarter to three. Each step creaks beneath your weight, and from above comes the soft tread of someone pacing, which stops whenever you stop. The foyer lies down below, and the stair climbs on to the upper landing.
rooms.1918: The stair ends on a broad landing, where a tall window black with grime looks over the dead garden. A long runner of faded carpet leads south down the hall, and doors stand east and west, each with a tarnished brass handle. Cold air pools around your ankles, and the banister seems to hum faintly under your hand. The stair goes down to the foyer.
rooms.1922: A small plain room with a narrow iron cot, a washstand and a row of pegs where black uniforms hang gone green with age. A mirror over the washstand is draped in a cloth that has fallen off and been replaced more than once. A connecting door south opens to the master bedroom, and the way west leads back to the landing.
rooms.1924: A vast four-poster bed dominates the room, its curtains moth-eaten and its mattress sunk in the middle as though someone were still lying there. Above the mantel hangs a portrait of a husband and wife whose smiles seem a little wider each time you look. A faint scent of lavender water hangs on the cold air. The maid's room lies north, a door south leads to a private sitting room, and an opening west gives onto the hall.
rooms.1926: A lady's private sitting room, lit by a dusty rose glow from a small stained-glass window, with a writing desk whose lock is broken, a faded chaise and a spinning wheel with a snapped thread. The cold at the window is so deep that the glass beads with moisture. Someone has been sitting on the chaise recently, for the cushion is dented. A way north returns to the master bedroom, and an opening west leads to the end of the hall.
rooms.1920: The hall ends in a blank wall hung with a cracked mirror in which the passage seems to run on longer than it does. Doors stand east and west, and the hall runs back north toward its center. From the rafters overhead comes the slow drag of something heavy across the boards, then silence.
rooms.1919: Portrait frames and closed doors line the walls of the hall, and the runner underfoot is worn to the boards. A hopscotch grid is chalked on the floorboards, the chalk fresh and white in the dust. The hall leads north to the top of the great staircase and south to its far end, with a door east to the master bedroom and another west to a child's room. A faint giggle echoes down the corridor, then stops.
rooms.1923: Peeling pink wallpaper, a small bed under a lace canopy and a dolls' house stand in this little girl's room, and a rocking horse faces the window with its painted eyes cracked. A music box on the shelf chimes thinly now and then, though its key is long gone. The air is cold and smells of lavender and wax. The only way out is the door east to the hall.
rooms.1925: A guest room prepared for visitors who never arrived: sheets gone yellow, a washbasin cracked from rim to base, a single candle stub in a dish. The window is nailed shut from the inside, and the nails are bright with fresh rust. A faint scratching comes from the wardrobe, and stops when you listen. A door east leads back to the end of the hall.
rooms.1921: A cramped closet fitted with a porcelain basin and a mahogany seat, the pull chain swinging a little in a draught that has no source. Cracked tiles line the walls, and a tap drips with a slow, patient rhythm. The mirror above the basin is fogged from the inside, and a finger has drawn a small face in it. The door east leads back to the landing.
rooms.1929: Brick vaults arch overhead in this old laboratory, where long benches of stained oak hold racks of glass, a rusted brass microscope and jars of dark liquid. An iron table with leather straps stands in the middle of the floor, its drain clogged with something black. The smell is of sour chemicals and cold stone. Stairs climb up to the grand foyer, and a pale green glimmer shifts in the jars when you move.
rooms.1930: The carnival's main gate is a tall arch of painted wood, its gilt letters flaking and its iron turnstiles rusted fast beneath it. Faded bunting droops from the beams, and a ticket booth stands shuttered, its glass cracked into a spider's web. Somewhere far off a calliope wheezes a few notes and stops. The midway opens north among the stalls, and behind you the road runs south toward the Eastern Gatehouse.
rooms.1931: The midway opens wide beneath a patchwork roof of rotting canvas, with stalls on every side under ruined awnings and the sawdust trampled to a grey crust. Faded paper lanterns sway on their wires without a breath of wind. Paths lead north toward the far end of the grounds, east to a hall hung with painted nymphs, west to a fortune-teller's booth, and south back to the gate.
rooms.1932: The midway narrows at this end into a lane of sagging booths, a ring-toss stall with its hoops long gone and a coconut shy with a ragged backdrop. Dried streamers hang from the canvas overhead, and a smell of old sugar and mildew lingers. A red-painted entrance glows dimly ahead to the north, a path runs east along the stalls, and west a broad hall bears a painted sign. The main grounds lie back south.
rooms.1937: This ride was built to look like the pit of hell, with black walls streaked with painted flames and red glass lanterns hanging dark on iron chains. A great demon's face of papier-mache gapes over the track, its jaws full of cracked teeth, and a rusted rail vanishes into the gloom behind it. The air is stale and tastes of tar and grease. The only way out is back south to the Northern End of the Carnival.
rooms.1933: Here the grounds bend around a cluster of striped tents, their canvas sagging and their ropes slack, the paint on their signs peeling away in long curls. Trampled straw and dry mud cover the ground, and a lopsided banner flaps in a draught. A path leads north to a caged lair, a tent lies east with a swordsman's sign, the main walk runs south, and a lane runs back west.
rooms.1939: A great cage wagon stands open here, its iron bars bent outward in places and thick with rust, and the floor is strewn with old straw gone black. Deep claw marks score the planking in sets of two, and a heavy musk still clings to the air. A painted board proclaims the beast within as the wonder of the age, though much of the paint has gone. A hatch north leads into the den, and the carnival lies south.
rooms.1942: The den is a low, dark box of planking at the back of the cage wagon, lined with old straw and stinking of animal. Two great hollows are pressed into the straw, side by side, where two heads once lay. Claws have gouged the walls to splinters in long, desperate stripes. The only way out is back south to the lair.
rooms.1940: A small striped tent shelters a raised stage with a faded scarlet curtain, and a rack of rusted swords stands upright in a stand beside it. A painted board lists the swallower's daring feats in flaking letters, and lamps with blackened chimneys line the footlights. Drifts of dust cover the sawdust floor, with one bare patch where a man might stand. The tent flap opens west to the carnival.
rooms.1938: Packed mud and scattered straw cover the ground between tattered tents on this side of the carnival, and a long row of empty benches faces a rickety stage. Glass bulbs on a string are dead along the edge of the canvas roof, and a mildew-coated wheel of fortune stands still. A path runs north toward the tents, east to a gaudy sideshow, and south to the main grounds.
rooms.1941: A row of curtained alcoves lines this sideshow, each with a painted banner hung above it that boasts of marvels long since vanished. The curtains hang in motionless folds, and cracked mirrors in gilt frames catch your reflection in odd, bent shapes. The air is close and hushed, and faint whispers rise from behind the cloth when you step. The only way out is west to the carnival grounds.
rooms.1936: A long hall of faded glory, its walls hung with portraits of vast, mustached strongmen and the iron dumbbells they hoisted. A tall high-striker stands in one corner, its bell cracked and its painted gauge worn down to the stub. The boards in the centre of the floor are scarred where weights have been dropped, and a trapdoor with an iron ring stands open to a stair leading down. The carnival lies east.
rooms.1943: A low cellar of earth and timber props stretches under the carnival, damp and cold, the floor beaten into black mud. Rotting crates stack against the supports, and the dim light from above shows only a few broken planks and dripping beams. A stair climbs up to the Strongman Hall of Fame, and a passage leads east into the dark.
rooms.1944: The passage is narrow and wet, its brick walls beaded with slime and its low ceiling dripping into puddles on the floor. Rusted pipes run overhead, and a smell of mould and stagnant water hangs heavy in the dark. Somewhere ahead, faint and tinny, a music box plays a jolting waltz. The passage runs east toward a painted doorway and west to the cellar.
rooms.1945: A huge painted face looms over the entrance to the fun-house, its mouth gaping as a doorway and its laughing eyes crossed with cracks. Warped mirrors line the walls on either side and bend you into long pale shapes with stretched limbs. The floor tilts under your feet, and a giddy, laughing music crackles from somewhere deeper in. The fun-house goes on east, and a passage returns west.
rooms.1946: Here the floor slopes and the walls lean, the whole room built to tip your balance, and a rotating barrel on its side blocks half the width. Mirrors of every shape cover the ceiling, so that countless faces peer down at you, all a little wrong. Plaster dust lies thick on the boards. A doorway north leads to a fallen room, another south opens on another, and the way west returns to the entrance.
rooms.1947: Half the ceiling has come down here in a fall of plaster, laths and splintered beams, burying one side of the room under a long grey slope. Painted stars on what remains of the roof show through the wreckage, and a cracked clown's head lies grinning in the rubble. Dust stirs in the still air. The only passable way is the doorway south to the entrance of the fun-house.
rooms.1948: The floor of this room has given way in the middle, leaving a ragged pit edged by broken joists and bent springs of the trick floor. Wallpaper in red and gold stripes peels from the wall in strips, and the mirror on the far side is a spiderweb of silver cracks. A chill breath rises out of the gap. The only safe way out is the doorway north.
rooms.1934: A round pavilion hung with painted nymphs who dance on the walls in a ring, their pale arms linked among garlands of dead flowers. The paint has peeled, and each nymph's face has gone blank as an egg. A little stage in the centre holds a ring of tarnished lamps, and a thin, sweet music seems to hum from nowhere. The way out is the curtained opening west to the carnival grounds.
rooms.1935: Heavy purple drapes cover the walls of this little booth, and a round table holds a crystal ball clouded like a cataract. Painted stars and moons crowd the ceiling, and the cards painted on the wall show a hanged man, a tower and a pale hand reaching from a cloud. The smell of incense is sharp and bitter. The curtain opening east leads back to the carnival grounds, and the table seems set for two.

1902.description: The family stares down in oils: a stern father, a pale mother, three children in Sunday dress, each face a little greyer than the last. Their eyes are bright, and they never rest on the same place twice.

1903.description: The ivory keys are yellow and chipped, and the dust on them lies in a perfect, undisturbed layer. Yet when you are not looking, the hammers sometimes stir.

1923.description: The dolls' house is a perfect copy of the great house, down to the tiny portraits in the foyer. A tiny figure stands in every room, and one stands at the open window of the little girl's room, facing out.

1928.description: The letters all begin 'Dearest' and end with the same few lines, repeated until the paper is black: let me out, let me out, it is so cold here.

1930.description: The gilt letters spell out a welcome to the finest carnival in the realm, and beneath them, in a different hand and newer paint, someone has added three words: we are waiting.

1945.description: In every warped glass you stand taller and thinner than you are, and now and then a second figure stands behind your shoulder, then vanishes as you turn.
